## Cause

The most recent commit, `4d99828` "Drop indexes with no recorded reads (Q3 storage review)", is the regression. It added `V3__drop_unused_indexes.sql`, which drops `ux_payment_idempotency_key` — the unique index added by `V2` specifically to close this bug.

The review's reasoning was that the index showed no reads in `pg_stat_user_indexes`. A uniqueness constraint never records reads: nothing plans a scan against it, the insert path enforces it. So it looked unused right up until it was the only thing preventing double charges. `V3`'s own comment says as much, but the `DROP` shipped anyway.

Without it, the only remaining guard is the application check in `PaymentService.java:29`:

```java
if (repository.existsByIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey)) {
```

That check races. Two concurrent requests with the same idempotency key both see "not present", both insert, both charge. `V2`'s comment (`PaymentService.java:20-25`) is explicit that this check is an optimisation and the index is the guarantee — dropping the index left only the half that races.

## Fix

Added `src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__restore_payment_unique_index.sql`, recreating the index, with a comment explaining why read statistics must not be used to judge it. I added a new migration rather than editing `V3` because `V3` is already applied in production and rewriting it would break Flyway's checksum.

`mvn test` passes, though the one existing test only covers `total()` and doesn't exercise this path.

## Before you deploy this

**The migration will fail if duplicates are already in the table.** `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` aborts on existing violations, so any payments double-charged since `V3` shipped have to be reconciled first. Worth running:

```sql
SELECT idempotency_key, count(*), sum(amount)
FROM payment GROUP BY idempotency_key HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

I haven't written a dedupe script — which duplicate row survives, and whether the extra charges get refunded or voided, is a call about real money that I'd want you to make. Happy to write it once you decide the rule.

Two things I noticed and deliberately left alone:

- **`ix_payment_status_created`, also dropped by `V3`, I did not restore.** It's an ordinary lookup index, so "no recorded reads" is sound evidence there. Restoring it is a performance question, not a correctness one.
- **The losing writer in a race now gets a `DataIntegrityViolationException`** surfaced to the GraphQL caller instead of the existing payment. That's pre-existing behaviour from `V2`, not new, and the failure is safe — one charge, one error. Catching it in `create` and returning the existing payment would make the mutation properly idempotent under contention. Outside the scope of this fix; say the word and I'll do it.
